entities.description: Black weekly (later daily) newspaper founded in Chicago in 1905; the central case of this brief.
entities.name: Chicago Defender

entities.description: Founder of the Chicago Defender (1905); publisher until his death in 1940.
entities.name: Robert S. Abbott

entities.description: Nephew of Abbott; part owner and general manager, later owner of the Defender and Sengstacke Enterprises.
entities.name: John H. Sengstacke

entities.description: Family holding company for the Defender and related properties; 70% owned by John H. Sengstacke at his death.
entities.name: Sengstacke Enterprises

entities.description: Media company that acquired the Defender from the Sengstacke trust in the 2002-2003 court-approved sale.
entities.name: Real Times LLC

entities.description: Black weekly published in Pittsburgh; used as a national comparison case for circulation trajectory.
entities.name: Pittsburgh Courier

entities.description: Chicago-based Black publishing company founded 1942; publisher of Ebony and Jet; used as a comparison case for the Black consumer-advertising model.
entities.name: Johnson Publishing Company

entities.description: Flagship monthly magazine of Johnson Publishing (1945); benchmark for Black consumer-magazine circulation and national-brand advertising economics.
entities.name: Ebony

entities.description: Weekly magazine launched by Johnson Publishing in 1951.
entities.name: Jet

entities.description: Founder of Johnson Publishing Company; oral history recorded by The HistoryMakers in 2004.
entities.name: John H. Johnson

entities.description: Defender headquarters at 3435 S. Indiana Avenue, Chicago, occupied beginning 1920; National Register-listed.
entities.name: Chicago Defender Building (3435 S. Indiana Ave.)

entities.description: Record company whose 'Race Record Artists Night' ad in the Defender (Feb. 6, 1926, p. 6) is primary evidence of entertainment advertising in the Black press.
entities.name: OKeh Records

entities.description: Radio manufacturer identified as Ebony's first major corporate advertising breakthrough.
entities.name: Zenith Radio Corporation

entities.description: The HistoryMakers video oral history program; recorded ~5h20m interview with John H. Johnson (Nov. 11, 2004); cataloged by NYPL.
entities.name: The HistoryMakers

entities.description: Annual parade founded by Abbott in 1929; the largest African-American parade in the U.S.; a Defender brand asset and audience engine.
entities.name: Bud Billiken Day

entities.description: Black street news vendors (1942 Delano photograph); retail distribution labor for the Defender.
entities.name: Defender newsboys / newsstand vendors

entities.description: Railroad workers who distributed the Defender across the South via the rail network; the physical infrastructure of the paper's national reach.
entities.name: Pullman porters
